title: Kanau Lite
description: A free app that turns an iPhone or iPad into one light, controlled over Art-Net or sACN. Getting started, lighting it by hand in CONTROL, modes and channels, FX & MEDIA, COOKIE and ULTIMATE, patching on a desk.
body:
Kanau Lite is a free app that turns an iPhone or iPad into one light. It receives DMX sent from a desk over Art-Net or sACN, and drives the color and brightness of the screen, the back light and the vibration. There is no account to create and there are no ads.

Without a desk, you can set the brightness and color in CONTROL and light it by hand. In the FX & MEDIA and ULTIMATE modes, the screen can also show moving patterns and your own images and videos.

What you need

  • An iPhone or iPad on iOS 17 or later.
  • To control it from a desk, a desk that sends Art-Net or sACN. Kanau or any other desk.
  • The same network as the desk, over Wi-Fi or a wired connection. The first time you open the app, it asks for Local Network access. Allow it.

Getting started

  1. Open Kanau Lite. The icon and the name show for a moment. Tap to skip them.
  2. The panel opens from the bottom of the screen, on SETUP. Kanau Lite starts this way each time it opens.
  3. Choose a Mode, then Art-Net or sACN, and set Universe and Address.
  4. Tap START at the bottom. The panel closes.
  5. From the desk, send DMX to that universe and address. When it arrives, the screen becomes the light.

Until you tap START, the screen does not light up, even if DMX arrives. To light it without a desk, tap CONTROL at the top of the panel instead of step 3, set the brightness and color, and tap START (see CONTROL).

The panel

The panel opens from the bottom of the screen, and the top third or so still shows the light. From the top, the panel has:

  • × at the top left, and two buttons, CONTROL and SETUP.
  • The DMX row (see DMX on and off).
  • While CONTROL is open, the LIGHT, MACRO and MEDIA buttons.
  • The contents of the chosen screen, and START at the bottom. START is in the same place on every screen.

To close the panel, tap START, tap × at the top left, or take the line at the top edge of the panel and swipe down. Each of these does the same as START.

To open the panel while the light is on, slide the faint switch at the top right all the way to the right, then tap EDIT. EDIT goes away after 3 seconds. Tapping the light or the address screen does not open the panel.

DMX on and off

Just below the two buttons of the panel is the DMX row. From the left: DMX ON and OFF, the address (for example U1 · 001), and the signal. The signal shows Receiving while DMX is arriving and No Signal while it is not.

While DMX is ON, the desk's light comes first whenever the desk is sending. While it sends, CONTROL is dimmed and cannot be tapped, and a line below says why and that turning DMX OFF lets you light it here. When the desk stops for 5 seconds, CONTROL works again, and tapping it switches to the light you set by hand. If the desk starts sending again, its light comes back.

With DMX OFF, Kanau Lite does not listen to the desk and always shows the light you set by hand. In SETUP, Art-Net / sACN, Universe and Address are dimmed and cannot be changed. They are kept, and work as before when you turn DMX back ON. The choice between ON and OFF is saved.

The address screen

After START, while DMX is ON and nothing has arrived yet, a black screen shows three lines in large type. This is the address screen. With many devices side by side, you can read each number from a distance.

  • The universe and address, in amber, for example U1 · 001.
  • The mode, for example 2: SCREEN RGB 9ch.
  • The network, this device's IP address and the protocol it listens for, for example Wi-Fi 192.168.1.24 · Art-Net. With no network, it shows No network.

Below them, a small line says how to open the panel. Tapping the address screen does nothing. While DMX is OFF, the address screen does not show, and the light you set by hand comes on instead.

CONTROL

CONTROL is where you set the brightness and color for lighting it by hand. It has three parts: LIGHT, MACRO and MEDIA. What you set is saved and is still there the next time you open the app. The sliders do not jump to where you touch; they move by as much as your finger moves.

LIGHT has:

  • Intensity: the brightness.
  • WHITE and COLOR: with WHITE, set the white with Color Temperature, the buttons 2700, 3000, 3200, 4300, 5600 and 6500, and Green / Magenta. Green / Magenta has magenta on the left and green on the right, and goes to 0 near the middle. With COLOR, set the color with Hue and Saturation.
  • Back Light: the brightness of the back light. A device without a back light does not show it.

While a pattern shows, ORIGINAL takes the place of WHITE. ORIGINAL is the pattern's own color. While a pattern, an image or a video shows, its name and STOP appear at the top of LIGHT. STOP stops the pattern and the image, leaving only the color set in LIGHT.

MACRO has:

  • Pattern: choose a pattern from the list. SOLID and nine moving patterns, the same as Content in FX & MEDIA below.
  • Color Macro: choose a color from the list. Original 1 to 3 are sets of colors that belong to the pattern, and are not listed for SOLID. FROM LIGHT is the color set in LIGHT, followed by 15 colors. Changing the color in LIGHT takes off the Color Macro color.
  • Speed, Amount and Size: the speed and the look of the pattern. They are dimmed while the pattern is SOLID.

In MEDIA, Media chooses an image or a video from the shelf (see Media). The list has Off and only the numbers that hold something. Play, Pause and Restart control playback, and each tap of Restart plays from the start again. While an image or a video shows, the color in LIGHT and all of MACRO are dimmed, and only Intensity and Back Light work.

SETUP

From the top:

ItemWhat it does
ModeShows the current mode, for example 2: SCREEN RGB 9ch. Tap it to choose from the modes below (see Modes and channels). The number at the start is the mode number. On a device without a back light, 1: BACK LIGHT ONLY is not listed, but the other modes keep their numbers.
Art-Net / sACNTap one of the two. The one you choose turns amber.
Universe0–32767 for Art-Net, 1–63999 for sACN.
AddressFrom 1 up to the highest address that still fits the mode's channels within 512.
ChannelsThe channels of the current mode (see below).
PROXIMITYWhen on, the screen goes dark while you hold this device to your ear. The back light and vibration keep going. It starts off. A device without a proximity sensor, such as an iPad, does not show it.
MediaShows how many of the 51 numbers hold an image or a video, for example 3 / 51. Tap it to open the shelf (see Media).
LanguageSystem, or one of 15 languages. The explanations change as soon as you choose. Names of items and buttons stay in English. Until you choose, Kanau Lite is in English.
GuideOpens a short guide in 8 steps. It is inside the app, so it works without the internet.

Type a number for Universe and Address, or use − and +. The amber line below them shows the addresses used by the screen, the back light and the vibration, for example Screen 001–007 · Back Light 008 · Vibration 009.

Each time you open SETUP, Channels starts folded and shows only the number of channels, for example 9ch. Tap the heading to open the list of the current mode's channels, with their address, name and what the values mean. The two lines on patching on Kanau and on other desks show even while it is folded. A row for a feature this device does not have (the back light or the vibration) is dimmed and starts with Not on this device. That row still uses its address, so count it on the desk too.

At the end of SETUP are the Kanau Lite version, Made by Kanau Labs, a link to kanaulabs.app, Privacy Policy, Contact Support, the Art-Net credit and the copyright. Settings are saved and are still there the next time you open the app.

While the light is on

The screen shows what it receives. While Kanau Lite is open, the screen stays at full brightness and does not lock automatically. If DMX from the desk stops, the light stays as it was.

When two desks send Art-Net to the same universe, Kanau Lite listens only to the one that arrived first. If that desk stops for 5 seconds, it listens to the other.

Kanau Lite receives DMX only while the app is open. If you go to the Home Screen or lock the device, it stops receiving, stops the back light and the vibration, and sets the screen brightness back to what it was. Open it again, and the last light comes back and it receives again.

Modes and channels

There are 19 modes. The default is 2: SCREEN RGB 9ch. The number at the start of each name is the mode number, and the number at the end is the number of channels.

ModeScreen
1: BACK LIGHT ONLY 1chUses the back light only. The screen stays dark.
2: SCREEN RGB 9ch
3: SCREEN HUE SAT 8ch		The whole screen is one color.
4: SCREEN 2 CELLS RGB 17ch
5: SCREEN 2 CELLS HUE SAT 15ch		The screen is split into 2.
6: SCREEN 4 CELLS RGB 31ch
7: SCREEN 4 CELLS HUE SAT 27ch		The screen is split into 4.
8: SCREEN 8 CELLS RGB 59ch
9: SCREEN 8 CELLS HUE SAT 51ch		The screen is split into 8.
10: SCREEN 4 STRIPS RGB 31ch
11: SCREEN 4 STRIPS HUE SAT 27ch		The screen is split into 4 strips along its long side.
12: SCREEN 8 STRIPS RGB 59ch
13: SCREEN 8 STRIPS HUE SAT 51ch		The screen is split into 8 strips along its long side.
14: SCREEN FX & MEDIA RGB 20ch
15: SCREEN FX & MEDIA HUE SAT 19ch		The whole screen, with patterns, images and videos (see FX & MEDIA).
16: SCREEN COOKIE RGB 62ch
17: SCREEN COOKIE HUE SAT 54ch		The screen is split into irregular, dappled areas in 8 colors (see COOKIE and ULTIMATE).
18: ULTIMATE RGB 74ch
19: ULTIMATE HUE SAT 66ch		Chooses how to split the screen, and shows patterns, images and videos (see COOKIE and ULTIMATE).

Apart from BACK LIGHT ONLY, every mode starts with Screen Dimmer and ends with Back Light and Vibration. 2: SCREEN RGB 9ch has these channels, in this order. The values are written as they appear in Channels in SETUP.

#NameValues
1Screen Dimmer0–100%
2CCT1,750–9,910 K · Home 117 = 5,494 K
3G/M0–4 No effect · 5 Magenta → 255 Green · Home 128
4Crossfade0 White → 255 Color · Home 0
5Red0–100%
6Green0–100%
7Blue0–100%
8Back Light0–100%
9Vibration0–100%

The HUE SAT modes have Hue (0–360°) and Saturation instead of Red, Green and Blue. In the CELLS and STRIPS modes, Screen Dimmer is followed by Dimmer, CCT, G/M, Crossfade and the color for each part of the screen. CELLS are numbered from the top left. With 8 cells, a portrait screen has 2 columns and 4 rows, and a landscape screen has 4 columns and 2 rows. STRIPS are strips of equal width placed along the long side of the screen. A portrait screen has horizontal strips numbered from top to bottom, and a landscape screen has vertical strips numbered from left to right. A square screen is split from top to bottom.

Crossfade sets the mix of white and color: 0 is white and 255 is color. The white comes from CCT and G/M. While Crossfade is at 0, raising Red, Green or Blue leaves the screen white. Screen Dimmer dims the screen only and does not affect the back light.

FX & MEDIA

14: SCREEN FX & MEDIA RGB 20ch has these channels, in this order. 15: SCREEN FX & MEDIA HUE SAT 19ch has Hue and Saturation instead of Red, Green and Blue.

#NameValues
1Screen Dimmer0–100%
2CCT1,750–9,910 K · Home 117 = 5,494 K
3G/M0–4 No effect · 5 Magenta → 255 Green · Home 128
4Crossfade0 White → 255 Color · Home 0
5Red0–100%
6Green0–100%
7Blue0–100%
8Color Macro0 Off · 5 Original 1 · 10 Original 2 · 15 Original 3 · 50–124 15 colors, 5 each · Home 0
9Content0 SOLID · 5 GLINT · 10 SWEEP · 15 KALEIDO · 20 WATER · 25 FIRE · 30 TV · 35 AURORA · 40 PAPARAZZI · 45 POLICE · Home 0
10Speed0 Slow · 128 Normal · 255 Fast · Home 128
11Amount0–255 · Home 128
12Size0–255 · Home 128
13Reserved 1Not used · Home 0
14Mix0 Media → 255 Pattern · Home 255
15Media0 Off · 1–5 = 1 · 6–10 = 2 … 251–255 = 51 · Home 0
16Playback0–85 Play · 86–170 Pause · 171–255 Restart · Home 0
17Color Temp0 Warm · 128 As is · 255 Cool · Home 128
18Reserved 2Not used · Home 0
19Back Light0–100%
20Vibration0–100%

The screen is built on black: first the image or video chosen by Media, then the pattern chosen by Content on top. Mix sets the balance: at 0 you see only the image or video, at 255 only the pattern. When Media is 0, or that number holds nothing, only the pattern shows. Reserved 1 and Reserved 2 are channels that do nothing.

The first value of Content, SOLID, fills the screen with color. Left at the defaults, FX & MEDIA gives the same light as SCREEN RGB. The other nine are moving patterns: Speed sets how fast they move, and Amount and Size change their look. Content 50–255 is unused and works as SOLID.

Each pattern has colors of its own, so it runs in a usable look even if you set no color. Crossfade at 0 shows the pattern's own colors, and at 255 the color from Red, Green and Blue.

Color Macro is split into steps of 5. Original 1 to 3, at 5–19, are sets of colors that belong to the pattern. From 50, in steps of 5, come these 15 colors: 3200 K, 4300 K, 5600 K, Red, Orange, Amber, Yellow, Green, Cyan, Sky Blue, Blue, Deep Blue, Lavender, Magenta, Pink. 0–4, 20–49 and 125–255 work as Off.

Images and videos keep their own colors. Color Temp shifts them warmer or cooler, and Screen Dimmer darkens them. Videos play without sound and loop from the start when they end. Playback plays or pauses the video. Restart sends the video back to the start once, at the moment the value enters 171–255.

COOKIE and ULTIMATE

SCREEN COOKIE splits the screen into irregular, dappled areas. Each area has the color of one of the 8 cells, so the color of one cell shows in several places on the screen. Some areas stay black whatever the cells are, so there is shadow between the light even with all 8 cells lit. For more shadow, set some of the cells to black on the desk.

16: SCREEN COOKIE RGB 62ch starts with Screen Dimmer, then Shape, Soft and Drift. Next come the 8 cells, each with Dimmer, CCT, G/M, Crossfade, Red, Green and Blue, as in the CELLS modes. Back Light and Vibration come last. 17: SCREEN COOKIE HUE SAT 54ch has Hue and Saturation in each cell instead of Red, Green and Blue.

#NameValues
2Shape0–255 Pattern · Home 0
3Soft0 Sharp → 255 Soft · Home 0
4Drift0 Still → 255 Fast · Home 0

Shape chooses the pattern. The pattern changes smoothly as the value moves, so a fade on the desk turns one pattern into the next. Soft blurs the edges between the areas: at 0 they are sharp. Drift sets how fast the pattern flows: at 0 it stands still.

18: ULTIMATE RGB 74ch has the channels of COOKIE, FX & MEDIA and 8 cells, in this order.

#NameValues
1Screen Dimmer0–100%
2Cells0 SCREEN · 32 2 CELLS · 64 4 CELLS · 96 8 CELLS · 128 4 STRIPS · 160 8 STRIPS · 192 COOKIE · Home 0
3–5Shape, Soft, DriftAs in COOKIE
6–16Color Macro, Content, Speed, Amount, Size, Reserved 1, Mix, Media, Playback, Color Temp, Reserved 2As in FX & MEDIA
17–72Dimmer 1 … Blue 87 channels for each cell, as in the CELLS modes
73–74Back Light, VibrationAs in the other modes

19: ULTIMATE HUE SAT 66ch has 6 channels for each cell, with Hue and Saturation, so the cells are 17–64 and Back Light and Vibration are 65–66.

The cells show only while Content is SOLID and Media is 0. Cells then chooses how the screen is split. SCREEN fills the whole screen with the color of cell 1. While a pattern, an image or a video shows (Content is not SOLID, or Media is not 0), the screen is one, as in FX & MEDIA, and the pattern takes its color and Crossfade from cell 1. Media counts by its value: a value other than 0 makes the screen one, even if that number holds nothing. Color Macro works only while the screen is one. While the screen is split, it has no effect. When Cells splits the screen into fewer than 8 parts, the channels of the other cells have no effect, but still use their addresses.

Media

The shelf holds images and videos on this device under the numbers 1 to 51. Open it from Media in SETUP. It is there in every mode, so you can fill it before you switch to FX & MEDIA or ULTIMATE.

  • Tap an empty number to add an image or a video from Photos or from Files.
  • Tap a number in use to replace what it holds, move it to another number, or delete it. If the other number is in use, the two swap.

On the desk, the Media channel picks the number: 1–5 is 1, 6–10 is 2, and so on, up to 251–255 for 51. The files stay on this device and are not sent anywhere.

Patching on a desk

On Kanau, patch this device as Kanau Lite with the same mode (chapter 03 of the manual). Kanau Lite in Kanau 1.1 has the same channels as Kanau Lite 1.1.

On other desks, make a fixture with the channels in the same order as Channels in SETUP, and patch it at the same address. Every channel is 8-bit.

A fixture patched to match Kanau Lite 1.0 has a different number of channels in modes 14, 15, 18 and 19, and different values for Color Macro and Content. Patch it again, on Kanau or on any other desk.

Over Art-Net, the app answers node discovery (ArtPoll) with a name such as Kanau Lite · U1 · 001. On a desk that can list nodes, look for this name, with its universe and address.

Contact

Write to info@kanaulabs.app in any language, or use Contact Support in SETUP. For a bug report, please include the Kanau Lite version shown at the end of SETUP, the mode you used, and your desk and protocol.
